title: 3. Distribution, Supply Chain & Unit Economics

epigraph.quote: In engineering services, your balance sheet is your bidding license, and your talent bench is your factory.
epigraph.author: Consulting Operations Maxim

web_blocks.text: Go-to-Market: PSU Nomination vs. Competitive Global Bidding

web_blocks.html: EIL wins work on two distinct tracks: domestic Public Sector Undertaking (PSU) jobs and global competitive tenders [3, 15]. At home, EIL holds deep ties with state energy majors IOCL, BPCL, HPCL, ONGC, GAIL, and NRL [3, 15]. It wins PSU orders through competitive bids and strategic nominations, such as underground crude oil caverns for ISPRL [3, 15]. EIL has engineered 20 out of 23 refineries and 11 out of 12 mega petrochemical complexes in India [3, 15]. That track record puts EIL at the table during early feasibility and licensor-selection studies, years before construction tenders open [3, 15].

Overseas, EIL cannot rely on PSU ties and must win on technical score and price [15]. To serve global clients, EIL runs an engineering hub in Abu Dhabi for ADNOC and Gulf national oil firms [3, 10]. It also opened an office in Saudi Arabia backed by a long-term services agreement (LTA) process with Saudi Aramco [3, 10]. Procurement and sales teams sit in London, Milan, and Shanghai [3, 10]. In Africa, EIL used its ten-year Dangote tie to win repeat multi-thousand-crore jobs in Nigeria and Ethiopia [3, 8, 10]. Government of India Lines of Credit (LoC) also helped EIL win refinery work in Mongolia and power and NGL oversight in Guyana [3, 8, 10].

web_blocks.text: Supply Chain, Manpower Bench & Subcontractor Risk

web_blocks.html: EIL's supply chain relies on skilled people rather than heavy plants [3]. As of March 31, 2025, EIL employed over 2,600 staff, including more than 2,300 engineers and technical experts [3]. That bench delivers roughly 3.5 million design-office man-hours and 1.3 million site-management man-hours each year [3]. Teams work across New Delhi, Gurugram, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Vadodara, and Abu Dhabi [3]. On Consultancy jobs, EIL's main inputs are internal engineers, design software, and R&D licensor ties [3, 6]. On Turnkey (LSTK) jobs, EIL manages external equipment makers, civil builders, and inspection teams, aided by subsidiary CEIL [7]. Because EIL owns no heavy yards or crane fleets, it avoids fixed depreciation drag. Still, it faces vendor delays, slow client sites, and contractor disputes on turnkey packages [13, 15].

web_blocks.text: FY26 Unit Economics: Where Every ₹100 of Revenue Goes

web_blocks.html: Tracing ₹100 of consolidated FY26 sales shows both EIL's asset-light core and its reliance on non-operating income [1]. On FY26 sales of ₹3,928 crore, subcontractors, gear, and materials took ₹46.08 per ₹100 [1]. Staff pay absorbed ₹26.22, and other operating costs took ₹9.90, leaving ₹17.80 in operating EBITDA (₹699 crore) [1]. Depreciation (₹1.07) and interest costs (₹0.13) are tiny [1]. Other Income—cash interest plus NRL and CIL dividends—added ₹6.16 per ₹100 (₹242 crore) [1, 15]. That lifted pre-tax profit to ₹22.76 and net profit to ₹17.62 (₹692 crore) [1, 15]. Operating cash flow hit ₹8.12 per ₹100 (₹319 crore), and low capex of ₹1.71 (₹67 crore) left ₹6.42 in free cash flow (₹252 crore) [1].

web_blocks.caption: FY26 Consolidated Unit Economics Waterfall (₹3,928 Cr Revenue; Expense Split Calibrated to Ind-AS Filings)
web_blocks.takeaway: Out of every ₹100 of FY26 sales, operating EBITDA kept ₹17.80 while treasury and dividend Other Income added ₹6.16. Working capital swings then reduced CFO to ₹8.12.

web_blocks.html: For an owner, EIL's unit economics act like a blend of a high-margin consultancy and a cash-rich treasury. Tiny capital spending (under 2% of sales) lets most operating cash flow turn into free cash flow. Yet the gap between FY26 net profit (₹692 crore) and operating cash flow (₹319 crore) shows how working-capital timing shapes real cash. Chapter 4 examines industry structure and EIL's moat, and Chapter 6 audits cash conversion in detail.

Billing terms also separate the two businesses. Consultancy contracts typically tie invoices to monthly man-hours or design milestones, keeping receivables tight [6][15]. Turnkey contracts often hold back 10% to 15% of contract value as retention money until plant commissioning [11][17]. When Turnkey revenue surges, unbilled contract assets rise on the balance sheet and delay operating cash flow [1][11]. Investors must therefore track debtor days and contract assets alongside reported profit margins [1][13].

book_paragraphs: To see how Engineers India Limited actually wins work and turns engineering hours into cash, you and I need to trace two very different sales channels. Inside India, EIL sits in an enviable position. Having engineered 20 out of India's 23 refineries and 11 out of 12 mega petrochemical complexes, EIL is the default technical advisor for state-owned energy giants like IOCL, BPCL, HPCL, ONGC, GAIL, and NRL. When the government plans a strategic underground crude oil cavern for ISPRL or a multi-billion-dollar refinery expansion, EIL is often brought in at the feasibility and licensor-selection stage—years before a construction tender is ever published.

Outside India, however, PSU incumbency counts for nothing. In the Middle East, Africa, and South America, EIL competes head-to-head against global engineering firms. To win there, EIL built an engineering hub in Abu Dhabi to serve ADNOC, operationalized an office in Saudi Arabia to pursue long-term service agreements with Saudi Aramco, and placed procurement and marketing teams in London, Milan, and Shanghai. When Dangote needed an engineering partner for its massive 650,000-barrel-per-day refinery in Nigeria, EIL won the EPCM mandate on technical credibility and cost competitiveness—and then parlayed that execution into repeat multi-thousand-crore expansion and fertilizer orders in 2026. Elsewhere, Government of India Lines of Credit opened doors for Mongolia's first oil refinery and Guyana's integrated NGL and 300 MW power plant.

book_subsections.title: An Asset-Light Factory of 2,300 Engineers
paragraphs: Unlike a manufacturing company that has to pour hundreds of crores into blast furnaces or CNC machines, EIL's factory walks out the front door every evening. Its core productive asset is a workforce of roughly 2,600 employees, including over 2,300 engineers and technical specialists, generating about 3.5 million design-office man-hours and 1.3 million construction-management man-hours each year across New Delhi, Gurugram, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Vadodara, and Abu Dhabi. Even on Turnkey EPC contracts, EIL does not own heavy cranes or pipe-bending yards; it designs the plant, procures equipment from global and Indian vendors, inspects quality through its subsidiary CEIL, and hires specialist subcontractors for site erection.

That human-capital structure explains why EIL's depreciation is barely ₹42 crore on nearly ₹4,000 crore of revenue, and why its capital expenditure in FY26 was just ₹67 crore. When consultancy orders surge, EIL can scale operating profit rapidly without taking on debt—because its existing engineering bench absorbs higher utilization. At the same time, you have to respect the operational constraint: you cannot double an engineering workforce overnight without diluting quality, and periodic PSU pay revisions can step up fixed employee costs.

book_subsections.title: The ₹100 Revenue Test
paragraphs: Walk with me through ₹100 of EIL's consolidated revenue in FY26, which totaled ₹3,928 crore. About ₹46.08 goes straight out the door to subcontractors, equipment suppliers, and project materials—mostly driven by the Turnkey segment. Another ₹26.22 pays for EIL's skilled engineering salaries, and ₹9.90 covers travel, software, and office overheads. That leaves ₹17.80 in operating profit before depreciation, or ₹699 crore across the year.

Now watch what happens below the operating line. Interest cost is virtually zero at ₹0.13 per ₹100 (₹5 crore), and depreciation is ₹1.07 (₹42 crore). Then comes a massive boost: ₹6.16 of Other Income—₹242 crore of interest earned on EIL's cash reserves plus dividends from Numaligarh Refinery and other investments. That lifts pre-tax profit to ₹22.76 and net profit to ₹17.62 (₹692 crore) after ₹5.14 in taxes. Yet when you look at the cash flow statement, only ₹8.12 per ₹100 (₹319 crore) arrived as operating cash flow in FY26 because working capital absorbed cash as project billing accelerated. After ₹1.71 in capex, EIL kept ₹6.42 per ₹100 in free cash flow (₹252 crore). Keeping your eye on that gap between accounting profit and cash conversion is essential before we examine EIL's competitive moat.

book_subsections.title: The Working Capital Trade-Off Inside the ₹100 Waterfall
paragraphs: Our FY26 ₹100 revenue-to-free-cash-flow waterfall highlights a subtle operational truth that headline profit margins obscure. On paper, EIL converted ₹100 of FY26 revenue into ₹17.60 of net profit—an impressive outcome for an engineering firm. Yet only ₹8.10 of that ₹100 arrived as operating cash flow, and ₹6.40 survived as free cash flow after capital expenditure. Where did the rest of the accounting profit go? It was temporarily absorbed by working capital—specifically unbilled contract assets and trade receivables as Turnkey and international projects scaled up.

In engineering contracting, milestone billing lags physical progress. When EIL completes 60 percent of a refinery package but the client's contractual payment milestone triggers at 75 percent completion, accounting rules allow EIL to book revenue today while cash waits in contract assets until tomorrow. For Consultancy contracts, receivables typically clear quickly; for Turnkey contracts, cash conversion can lag by quarters. Tracking CFO-to-PAT conversion alongside debtor days is therefore essential whenever Turnkey revenue surges.

book_subsections.title: Nomination Versus Competitive Bidding: How EIL Wins Work
paragraphs: A common misconception among outside investors is that EIL receives all of its domestic PSU orders automatically without competition. In reality, EIL's go-to-market engine operates on two distinct tracks: strategic nomination for specialized brownfield revamps and national-security energy infrastructure, and competitive international bidding for greenfield refineries, LNG terminals, and overseas EPC packages.

On nominated domestic jobs, pricing is typically structured on cost-plus or fixed-fee man-hour schedules, which protects EIL from raw material inflation and keeps Consultancy margins predictable. On competitive international tenders—such as the Dangote refinery expansion or Middle East FEED mandates—EIL wins by combining lower Indian engineering man-hour costs with a 60-year refinery track record. Understanding which track a new order belongs to is the key to forecasting whether backlog growth will translate into high-margin cash or working-capital drag.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: The Hidden Weight of Other Income
book_callouts.text: When treasury interest and dividends supply ₹6.16 out of every ₹22.76 of pre-tax profit, they act as a shock absorber in lean years—but they can also flatter the business during boom years. Always separate core engineering profit from treasury yield.
